items.description: Однострочное сообщение под полем формы: точка тона и фраза. Ни заголовка, ни описания — второй уровень текста в таком месте не читают.

  onCancel={close}

ai.summary: An irreversible-action confirmation: a heading in the danger tone, a list of what will be lost, a field for typing the object's name and two buttons. While the field is empty the confirm button is disabled by a CSS rule — no JS involved. Zero dependencies, one file, its own palette.
preserve: the local --vibeui-alert-020-* palette — do not swap it for your theme tokens (bg-destructive and the like)
light-dark() in the palette: the component has to follow the surrounding color-scheme rather than ship a dark theme of its own
the transparent background by default — the component sits on the page background instead of laying a panel under itself
typing the name as the pause before something irreversible: that is what separates a stray click from a decision
the list of losses above the field: it has to be read before the typing starts
itemised losses rather than "all data": specifics are the only thing that makes people stop
the :has(input:placeholder-shown) rule that disables confirm without JS, and the space placeholder it rests on
role="alertdialog" and the aria-label carrying the heading
the <style> block inside the component — it holds the palette and the disabling logic
adapt: the title, description, inputLabel and button copy
confirmWord — what has to be typed; usually the object's name
losses — what will disappear
onCancel — dismissal; handle confirmation on the form's submit
width and outer spacing through className
background — the component background; empty means no background, taking the page colour
notes: The theme comes from color-scheme. For the component to darken with the system, the project must declare color-scheme: light dark on html — otherwise light-dark() always returns the light branch.
Verify the exact match on the server: pattern and CSS are convenience, not protection.
The component does not wrap itself in a <form>: the wrapper and the submit handler come from the caller.
Do not ask people to type "DELETE": the object's name forces a look at what is being deleted, while a fixed word is typed without reading.
Do not lift the CSS variables into globals.css: the component has to stay a single file.

While the field is empty the confirm button is unavailable — this is done by the `:has(input:placeholder-shown)` rule, that is, without a single line of JS.
